svg.text: The jitter landscape: twenty-one dimensions, and its map
Left: one ribbon per dimension n from 1.5 to 6.5; the vertical axis is the local exponent, and the grey dashed line under each ribbon is that dimension's mean (n - delta)/2.

Right: the same terrain from above. Colour is the local exponent, diverging about the critical slope 1. The straight line is the mean crossing at n = 2 + delta = 4.7; the white curve is the realised one.
the faint floor is slope 1, the critical level
the white curve is the realised frontier
realised frontier: where the local exponent crosses 1
Left: ribbons coloured by their MEAN, so the blue-to-red progression is the classification; the wiggle about each grey dashed mean line is the jitter depth.
Right: the same terrain from above. The straight black line is exact, n = 2 + delta; the width of the white curve's wander about it is the jitter depth.
The roughness is synthetic — the real jitter statistics are not known to me.
Exact: the mean plane (n - delta)/2, its crossing of slope 1 at n = 2 + delta, and the depth as the vertical gap.
